candidates.source_name: MNB Határozatok és végzések keresése (hatarozatkereso.mnb.hu)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory publication platform for every MNB supervisory decision (határozat) and order (végzés): licensing, enforcement (jogérvényesítés), market supervision (piacfelügyelet) and consumer protection (fogyasztóvédelem), filterable by date, sector and decision type. This is the canonical primary record of how Hungarian banking/payments rules are actually enforced, including fines on banks, payment institutions and e-money issuers.
candidates.legal_status: official public-sector information published under statutory disclosure obligation
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the search interface with date-range + decision-type filters; capture decision PDFs and their H-XXX-YYY reference numbers; diff against last run. Check for a JSON/XHR endpoint behind the search form before HTML scraping.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on MNB sanction terms, then fetch of the MNB landing page which points to hatarozatkereso.mnb.hu

negative_findings.description: No RSS feed, open API, bulk export or documented result-URL pattern was found for the MNB decision search (hatarozatkereso.mnb.hu). The MNB landing page documents filters and numbering but not any machine interface.
negative_findings.result_summary: Collection will likely require HTML/XHR scraping of a JavaScript search form rather than a clean feed; ingestion cost and breakage risk are higher than for GVH or NAIH.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single most important enforcement register in the cell; if it cannot be reliably automated, coverage of MNB sanctions degrades to press-release monitoring, which omits smaller and non-publicised decisions.

negative_findings.description: PBT (Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület) publishes only its binding decisions and recommendations, anonymised and with a short summary — not the full case file, and not settlements-by-agreement in detail.
negative_findings.result_summary: The public PBT register is a partial, redacted view of the complaint landscape; the quantitative picture must come from the annual reports rather than from counting published items.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Under-counting complaint volumes or mis-reading dispute mix would distort the 'issues before they become rules' early-warning function this cell exists to serve.

negative_findings.description: Neither the NAIH decision register nor the BHGY court-decision collection offers a financial-sector or NACE-style filter; both must be mined by keyword.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank/PSP-relevant items must be isolated with a Hungarian keyword list (bank, hitelintézet, pénzforgalmi szolgáltató, bankkártya, követeléskezelő, fizetési megbízás), accepting recall/precision trade-offs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Keyword-only retrieval will miss cases where the controller or litigant is named without sector wording, so enforcement counts from these sources are lower bounds.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, consolidated Hungarian register of court challenges against MNB supervisory decisions (i.e. outcomes of közigazgatási per against felügyeleti bírság) was found as a standalone product; such rulings are dispersed inside BHGY/Kúria and must be reconstructed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched in Hungarian for the anonymised-decision collections; found general-purpose portals only, no MNB-specific litigation tracker.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Whether sanctions survive judicial review is the strongest evidence of how durable a supervisory position is; without a tracker this must be assembled case by case.

negative_findings.description: Several useful commentary/aggregation layers are commercial: Wolters Kluwer Jogtár, Vixio Regulatory Intelligence, and partially Portfolio and Adózóna.
negative_findings.result_summary: These offer better-structured enforcement digests than free sources but require subscriptions; free primary registers remain sufficient for the core record.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Budget decision: subscribing buys speed and structure, not unique primary facts.

negative_findings.description: Only one URL in this slice was fetched directly (the MNB decision-search landing page). All other URLs come from search-result metadata and are recorded as unverified pending the deterministic liveness pass. One slug in particular (otthonapenzugyekben.hu …/panaszkezelas/) is transcribed from a search result and may be misspelled or moved.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs supplied with confidence scores, not liveness claims.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents downstream treatment of scouted URLs as verified endpoints.

coverage_gaps.description: No source found yet for enforcement/complaint activity at the payment-scheme and infrastructure layer (GIRO Zrt. / instant payment system AFR incident and dispute handling, card scheme arbitration outcomes in HU).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted hu searches on 'azonnali fizetési rendszer AFR incidens', 'GIRO Zrt. üzemzavar', 'kártyatársasági chargeback vitarendezés' and check MNB payment-system oversight (felvigyázás) publications.

coverage_gaps.description: Payment fraud and authorised push payment (APP) dispute/liability enforcement was not separately scouted; the emerging PSR/PSD3 reimbursement debate will make this the dominant complaint category.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search hu for 'csalás áldozata visszatérítés bank MNB állásfoglalás', 'jóvá nem hagyott fizetési művelet visszatérítés', and en for 'Hungary APP fraud reimbursement supervisory expectation'.

coverage_gaps.description: Pointer sources for aggregated EU-level enforcement touching HU banks/PSPs (EBA breach-of-Union-law and peer-review outputs, EDPB one-stop-shop decisions, CJEU preliminary rulings originating from Hungarian courts) were identified only indirectly via the C-630/23 reference.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add EBA, EDPB and CURIA case-law search as standing pointer sources filtered on Hungary and on financial/payment subject matter.

coverage_gaps.description: The historical depth of hatarozatkereso.mnb.hu, the PBT recommendation register and the NAIH pre-GDPR archive was not established, so multi-year trend feasibility is unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: During the first collection run, probe the earliest retrievable date in each register and record it as a dataset property.

coverage_gaps.description: English coverage of Hungarian enforcement is thin and selective: MNB English pages exist for supervision and investor warnings, and sanctioned institutions occasionally publish English decision translations, but neither GVH decisions, NAIH decisions, PBT recommendations nor BHGY court rulings are systematically available in English.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for machine translation of Hungarian primary text as a pipeline stage rather than relying on English-language sourcing; keep hu originals as the authoritative record.

brief: Hungary's enforcement and dispute landscape for banking/payments is unusually centralised: the MNB is simultaneously prudential supervisor, financial consumer-protection authority, market-supervision body and host of the Pénzügyi Békéltető Testület, so hatarozatkereso.mnb.hu, the MNB press room, the piacfelügyelet/figyelmeztetés registers and the PBT ajánlások/kötelezések pages together carry the bulk of the primary record. Around that core sit three adjacent enforcers with their own public decision databases — GVH (Versenytanács decisions plus a live 2026 investigation into bank card terminal operators), NAIH (GDPR decisions against financial controllers), and the courts via BHGY and the Kúria's jogegységi határozatok, which determine whether supervisory positions and consumer-contract practices actually hold. All primary material is Hungarian-only with no discovered API or RSS on the most important register, so collection is scraping-plus-translation work; English exists only as MNB summaries, occasional institution-published decision translations, and compliance trade media. The main residual risks are recall (no sector filters in NAIH/BHGY, keyword mining required) and two unscouted areas — payment-fraud/APP reimbursement disputes and the scheme/infrastructure layer — both flagged as gaps.
